subject: sociology

moments.title: The Division of Labour in Society
moments.body:
Durkheim distinguishes mechanical solidarity (similarity-based) from organic solidarity (interdependence-based).

He argues modern societies cohere through specialised, mutually dependent roles.
moments.takeaway: Modernity needs a sociology because it produces a new kind of social bond.

moments.title: Le Suicide
moments.body:
Durkheim shows suicide rates correlate with religion, marital status and wartime, arguing the phenomenon is a 'social fact'.

Later critics (Douglas, 1967) question whether 19th-century coronial records are robust enough to support the analysis.

quote.text: There can be no sociology unless societies exist, and societies cannot exist if there are only individuals.

moments.takeaway: Sociology stakes its independence from psychology by showing patterns no individual story explains.

moments.title: The Elementary Forms of Religious Life
moments.body: Durkheim treats religion as society's reflection on itself, drawing on Aboriginal Australian ethnography (which he himself never conducted).
moments.takeaway: Foundational theory in sociology often relied on second-hand ethnographic sources.

now.title: Sociology of the social bond today
now.body: Contemporary scholars use Durkheimian frameworks to study loneliness, online community and political polarisation. Suicide research integrates sociological and clinical data.
now.open_questions: How do digital platforms reshape integration and regulation? Are anomic conditions identifiable in contemporary data?

reflection: Durkheim wrote during the founding of the French Republic; his concerns about social cohesion echo current public debates.
